newsitem.title: USA: May shareholder launches proxy contest.
newsitem.headline: May shareholder launches proxy contest.

text.p: A union shareholder group said Thursday it has launched a proposal that would force May Department Stores Co to rescind its poison pill rights plan.

The Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees (UNITE) said it is not aware of any pending bids for May but its proposal is aimed at giving shareholders a stronger voice in the department store chain's future should an offer emerge.
The union will present the plan for a vote at the company's annual meeting May 23.

St. Louis-based May said it will recommend shareholders vote against the proposal and two others seeking a change in the company's bylaws so that directors are elected annually instead of staggered terms and requesting May beef up its code of conduct for vendors.
In a statement, May said the proposal did not appear in proxy statements sent to shareholders last month because it was not required to do so. It did not elaborate.
The proposal to eliminate the poison pill is unusual because it would be a binding measure that would not require approval from May's directors if shareholders ratify it, UNITE said.
The union said UNITE pension trusts own 53,418 shares of May stock.
